newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate tax offer doesn't move on big issues.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate tax offer doesn't move on big issues.

text.p: The first counteroffer by senators negotiating the tax bill with the House of Representatives did not include movement on any of the major items, but resolved a number of smaller issues. A copy of the counteroffer was obtained by Reuters on Thursday.

The Senate side of the bargaining table stuck by its provisions on the $500 per-child tax credit, higher education incentives, expansion of Individual Retirement Accounts, estate tax relief and the capital gains tax cut.
Lawmakers are trying to iron out differences in tax cut bills passed by the Senate and House to craft a single bill.
The Senate counteroffer also stuck to its position of seeking a 20-cents per pack tax increase on cigarettes, which is not included in the House bill.

The Senate proposed yielding to the House on a plan to charge a $15.50 per passenger international arrival and departure fee, with the caveat of keeping current law for domestic flights to and from Alaska and Hawaii. Currently there is an international departure fee of $6 per passenger.
The Senate stayed with its position on the ethanol subsidy of extending it but at reduced levels after 2000, while the House bill proposes eliminating it after 2000.

The Senate proposal showed agreement with the House on some smaller issues such as delaying imposition of penalties on small businesses for failing to make payments of certain taxes to Treasury electronically to after June 30, 1998.

Agreement was also shown for the effective date for allowing computer software licensed for reproduction abroad to receive an export benefit that would allow a portion of the foreign trade income to be exempt from federal income tax. The effective date would be after December 31, 1997.

Another point of agreement was to reduce the tax rate on apple cider having an alcohol content of no more than seven percent to 22.6 cents per gallon, the same as for beer produced by small breweries. Currently cider is taxed at the same rate as wine of $1.07 per gallon.

Agreement was also shown on replacing an 11 percent manufacturers' tax on assembled arrows that are either longer than 18 inches or are used with bows subject to tax with a 12.4 percent manufacturers' tax on four arrow components.
